t: In the question given below, four statements are given which may or may not contain an error. Choose the one that is grammatically and meaningfully correct.

I want to sea the beautiful views of the coast.
Turn the light on so I can sea.
I couldn't believe my eyes when I saw a see.
e:
Among the given sentences, only sentence a) is error free.
Sentence b): The verb "see" should be used after the infinitive marker "to", instead of the noun "sea".
Sentence c): The modal verb "can" should be followed by the base verb "see", instead of the noun "sea".
Sentence d): The indefinite article "a" is always followed by the noun. So, the verb "see" should be replaced by the noun "sea".

Note:
An infinitive marker is a word or affix that indicates that a verb is in its infinitive form. The most common infinitive marker is "to", which is used before the base form of a verb. For example, "to make" is an infinitive with the infinitive marker "to".
